# Casella Public Beta in Malaysia — 3-Day Simulated Dialogue: Predicted Reactions, Behaviors and Risks

> In a 3-day simulation across Twitter and Reddit, Malaysian homeowners, appliance buyers, inspiration browsers, cautious first‑time guests, local merchants, creators and professionals reacted to Casella’s public beta with cautious curiosity: many say they would try it when prices and total landed cost are clear, merchants view merchant portal features as promising but expect lead quality proof, and privacy, transparency and verification emerge as primary friction points requiring real‑world testing.

---

## Macro state after 3 simulated days

**Overall macro state after three simulated days**

The simulated public-beta launch produced a clear pattern: cautious curiosity combined with active verification behaviour. Communities and creators amplified a common checklist (total landed cost, labelled ads, privacy controls, match accuracy) while small merchants evaluated the merchant portal on ROI and lead quality. The tone across agents was constructive but wary: many will try Casella’s guest scans, far fewer will commit money until landed costs, ad-labelling and privacy are proven. This chapter synthesises the simulation evidence into predicted behaviors, shared frictions, and priority tests.

**Representative evidence of behaviours and intent**

Many agents said they would use the 3 free guest scans but stop short of signing in or buying until more transparency appears:

> "Guests get 3 free scans without an account, and saving items or a 4th scan asks them to sign in with Google, Apple, phone OTP or email."  

Several cautious users described an explicit guest-first routine and a gatekeeping posture toward permissions and retention:

> "Priya Nair reminds people to do a guest scan before signing in, reject unreasonable location permissions, check language settings and make sure data can be deleted."

> "Priya Nair's daily reminders are: check before you click, use guest mode first instead of rushing to register, reject location permission without reason, check the language and make sure data can be deleted..."

Technical and fit failures from early testing produced fast rejections by some appliance buyers and creators:

> "Kevin Lim ... deleted the app in 2 minutes" (after a mismatched first result).

> "Ah Boon Fix It tested the Casella beta as a creator."  
> "Ah Boon Fix It ... match accuracy is hit-or-miss, ... photos can be deleted but the option is buried 3 menus deep with no 'delete all'; the buy button opens Shopee/Taobao, making seller, courier and warranty holder three different parties."

Merchants reacted conditionally: openness to the merchant portal but insistence on metrics and clear advertising labels:

> "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya reacts to the announced merchant portal, including its verification, product listing, local-first matching, leads, dashboards, quotes and Partner slot."

> "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya said the Partner slot looks useful but it needs clear ROI metrics first, asking how to see when a link actually pays."

Creators and creators’-rights advocates demanded consent, credit and labelled affiliate links before endorsing or uploading images:

> "Priya Nair demands creator credit and compensation with explicit consent for listings, demos and AI training."

> "Nadia Home Diary ... refuses to hide commissions: every link gets an 'iklan'/'Link affiliate' label before the click, ... because 'disclosure is a relationship, bukan disclaimer.'"

**Which persona groups say they will try, return to, or leave — and why**

- Try (conditional, likely one-off or exploratory): inspiration browsers, creators testing content, many cautious first-time guests. Evidence: repeated references to the 3 free scans and guest-mode testing (see Priya Nair quotes and the 3-free-scans rule).

- Return (possible with proofs): homeowners and appliance buyers who see consistent, itemised total landed cost, verified delivery by postcode and reliable match accuracy. Evidence: repeated insistence that the "Best offer" must be based on total landed cost and that sellers list delivery and installation line items.

- Leave / uninstall: users encountering immediate mismatches, hidden fees, or opaque privacy/retention terms (e.g., Kevin Lim’s two‑minute deletion and Ah Boon Fix It’s match failures). Evidence: Kevin Lim’s behaviour and Ah Boon Fix It’s report on buried delete controls.

**How key product elements drive behaviour**

- Tagged room prices / Best offer (total landed cost): The dominant demand is for itemised landed cost, not sticker price. Multiple agents insisted the badge be unbuyable and computed on a full landed-cost formula.

> "Malaysia Reno Kaki ... says its Best offer badge is based on total cost including delivery, installation and import charges, not just the sticker price."

> "Budget Reno Bro ... 'Harga app vs harga kedai, bro.'"

> "Sinar Home Marketplace ... says the 'Best offer' badge must never be buyable and must stay on total landed cost (unit, delivery, installation, after-sales) and seller trust."

Expected behaviour: users will scan to shortlist but cross-check prices on Shopee/Taobao or local shops before paying. Many will screenshot or record the claimed landed cost and call shops for confirmation.

- Guest scans and privacy controls: Guest mode reduced friction for exploration, but retention and delete semantics are gating factors. Users systematically tested delete and permission flows (plant-photo habit) and refused to upload real-room photos until retention is explicit.

> "Priya Nair tested Casella's guest scan by denying the location permission at the OS level and found the scan still worked, which she says shows the permission was never necessary."

> "Chua Li Ting will not scan a single room unless retention terms are written clearly (hitam putih)..."

Expected behaviour: high initial scan volume from cautious browsers; low conversion to saved rooms or accounts until retention and delete are plainly stated and testable.

- Merchant portal, paid Partner slot, leads and affiliate links: Merchants are open to the portal but require ROI transparency, lead qualification and clear ad labelling. Creators require consent and commission disclosure for their images.

> "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya asks that the paid Partner slot show clear ROI metrics so the shop can justify every ringgit and see when a link actually pays the app."

> "Azlan Musa says that if there is a paid Partner slot, it must be clearly labelled as an advertisement."

> "Malaysia Reno Kaki ... calls transparency non-negotiable."

Expected behaviour: merchants will provisionally list and test small; many will hold back budget for paid slots until cost-per-qualified-lead is published and lead verification exists.

**Platform signals and where discussions concentrated (simulation-derived)**

The simulation produced platform-specific signal differences to the extent captured in the search results (use these phrases only as evidence where present). Across the simulated corpus the term "landed" had large presence on both platforms, and privacy/delete concerns were frequent. The overall medians and term shares in the simulation show both platforms engaged deeply (do not infer cross-platform influence).

**Key disagreements and friction points (with exact quotes)**

- Price transparency vs convenience: some users welcomed quick tagged prices but demanded detailed landed-cost line items.

> "Budget Reno Bro scanned a living room ... for a total landed cost of RM 327."  

> "Rumah Lengkap Marketing posted that Casella beta is a nice idea but a photo tag is not a quote..."  

- Advertising monetisation vs editorial neutrality: merchants and community moderators demanded upfront iklan labelling and that Partner slots not receive Best offer badges.

> "The Casella merchant phase includes one paid Partner slot per list that cannot receive the Best offer badge."

> "Wong Kar Fai says a paid Partner slot must be labelled clearly as advertising, front and centre and not in small print."

- Privacy / data retention vs model improvement: creators and cautious users want clear delete semantics and consent for reuse; product teams may need images for training.

> "Grace Chin says ... testing the delete button with a plant photo before uploading a real home is the best point in the thread because room photos are not free data."

> "Priya Nair says that if you can't find a permanent delete or a clear data-retention period in the Casella app, treat it as a no."

These conflicts predict a slow ramp: exploration is high, sustained conversion depends on resolving these tensions.

**Top risks the simulation surfaced**

1. Trust risk from mismatches and incomplete landed costs — users who see a wrong match or hidden fees uninstall quickly (Kevin Lim, Ah Boon Fix It evidence).
2. Privacy risk from unclear retention and delete flows — several agents refused to upload real-room photos until deletion is verifiable (Chua Li Ting; Priya Nair).
3. Reputation/compliance risk if paid placements are not clearly labelled — communities demanded iklan labelling up‑front; undisclosed affiliate links would erode trust.
4. Merchant churn risk if partner-slot ROI and lead quality are not transparent — small shops will test only after seeing cost-per-qualified-lead (Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya).

**Opportunities the simulation surfaced**

- High trial engagement via guest scans: 3 free scans encourage broad sampling and social sharing by creators.
- Creator-led education and disclosure norms (CreditCreators): creators can drive adoption if consent, credit and labelled affiliate links are standard.
- Local-first merchant matching and verified listings: convincing local merchants to publish full landed costs can create a competitive advantage in East Malaysia and small-shop audiences.
- Lead verification and dashboard transparency as merchant acquisition levers: publish cost-per-qualified-lead and lead-conversion metrics to win small retailers.

**Suggested user tests (labelled as suggestions)**

- Suggestion: Run a disclosure-timing A/B test (two flows) to see whether labelling affiliate links and Partner slots before the click increases trust and click-throughs among creators and community moderators.

- Suggestion: Conduct a privacy-delete usability test with real users (plant-photo protocol): participants try guest scans, deny location, attempt permanent delete, and then rate trust and willingness to upload a real-room photo.

- Suggestion: Benchmark match accuracy with a labelled test set (top-1 category accuracy and precision@1 on exact model code) across common Malaysian items (rattan, kolam rugs, AC indoor/outdoor model codes) and publish the results.

- Suggestion: Run a small paid‑slot pilot with a cohort of local merchants that includes transparent cost-per-qualified-lead reporting and lead verification; measure merchants’ willingness to pay and retention over 30 days.

- Suggestion: Cross-check "Best offer" badge calculations with live buyers across postcodes (Peninsular vs Sabah/Sarawak) to verify whether posted landed totals match actual checkout/delivery/installation invoices.

**Concluding prediction**

After three simulated days, Casella is positioned for exploratory uptake but must address three non-negotiables to move from curiosity to repeated use: (1) verifiable itemised total landed cost by postcode, (2) clear, upfront labelling of any paid placements and affiliate commissions, and (3) transparent, testable privacy and deletion controls (guest-mode delete must be demonstrable). If those elements are validated in the real world, the simulation predicts conditional return behavior from homeowners, merchants' measured adoption, and creator-led amplification. If not, the dominant outcome will be rapid trial followed by abandonment and vocal community scepticism.

## How major Agent groups responded and their stated intentions

**Summary of major groups' stated intentions**

Across the three simulated days the pattern repeated: many agents said they would "try" Casella conservatively (mostly via the 3 free guest scans), a subset said they would "return" only after clear, itemised total landed costs and verified match accuracy, and some said they would "leave" quickly when first matches or privacy controls failed. The evidence below is drawn from simulated agent posts and comments.

**Homeowners planning renovation — cautious conditional returners**

- Many homeowners framed Casella as a discovery tool only, and said they would reuse it if the platform showed itemised landed cost and postcode-accurate delivery days.
  
  > "Malaysia Reno Kaki posted that Casella has opened a public beta in Malaysia and says its Best offer badge is based on total cost including delivery, installation and import charges, not just the sticker price."  
  
  > "Lim Wei Jie says the 'Best offer' badge must be computed on total landed cost itemised as unit price, delivery, installation and warranty terms covering parts and labour and local authorised unit versus parallel import."

- Stated intention: try as exploration; return if the "Best offer" equals a verifiable total landed cost and delivery by postcode is shown.

  Evidence of this conditional posture appeared repeatedly:

  > "Budget Reno Bro posted a weekend check-in for homeowners and renovators of Sabah and Sarawak advising them to check local suppliers first and compare total landed cost."  

  > "Amirah Zulkifli says Casella is finally an app that shows total cost and not just the sticker price, and that the Best offer badge would be worth trying if it really includes delivery and installation."

**Appliance replacers — evidence-driven testers who will leave on mismatch**

- Appliance buyers demanded SKU/model-code level proof and itemised installation and warranty terms before committing; they reported immediate app deletion when early matches were wrong.

  > "Kevin Lim quoted Budget Reno Bro's post about the Casella public beta and commented that he is trying the 3 free scans only, with no account."  

  > "Kevin Lim plans to measure first and then test Casella, and will delete Casella unless the first result is correct and has real reviews and delivery days."  

  > "Faizal Rahim says that before trusting the Best offer badge he needs to know whether the total cost includes delivery, standard installation (piping, brackets, labour), and import tax, or is sticker price only."

- Stated intention: try guest scans; leave quickly on a wrong first match or opaque totals; return only after reliable, itemised landed-cost quotes and verified match accuracy.

  Supporting evidence:

  > "Wong Kar Fai posted that Casella announced a later merchant phase for Malaysian stores with verified listings, local stores matched first, a leads inbox, a dashboard, and one paid Partner slot per list that cannot receive the Best offer badge, not available during the beta."

**Inspiration browsers — frequent try, low purchase intent unless landed cost convinces**

- Inspiration browsers treat Casella like an inspiration feed; many will use the free scans repeatedly but rarely buy unless total landed cost and fit are confirmed.

  > "Tiffany Yeoh plans to test Casella's 3 free scans on her Japandi inspiration and report back."  

  > "Hannah Lau said Casella's 3 free scans sound dangerous for her virtual dream home folder."  

  > "Hannah Lau quoted Budget Reno Bro's post about the Casella app and commented that she scans everything and saves all the inspo but never buys."

- Stated intention: try and save (within guest limits), return as an inspiration tool; unlikely to convert without clearer landed costs and recognition fidelity.

**Cautious first‑time guests — trial-first, privacy‑driven behavior**

- Cautious guests repeatedly relied on guest scans and privacy checks; many explicitly tested deletion on dummy photos and refused to scan real home photos until retention was clear.

  > "Priya Nair prefers to wait and observe, reading before trusting, just as she tests guest scan before signing in."  

  > "Priya Nair reminds people to do a guest scan before signing in, reject unreasonable location permissions, check language settings and make sure data can be deleted."  

  > "Chua Li Ting asks whether she can try the app as a guest without signing in with her real name, and says she will not scan a single room if the retention period isn't clear."

- Stated intention: try the 3 free guest scans; leave or not upload real-home photos if retention/deletion and use-for-AI concerns are unresolved; may return only if privacy and delete controls pass simple in‑app tests.

  Example behavioural rule reported:

  > "Lau Kok Wai asks where room photos go, how long they are kept, whether deletion is actually permanent, and whether the guest scan works without an account or a phone number."

**Local merchants — cautious sign‑ups, ROI-first portal evaluation**

- Merchants welcomed the merchant portal concept but conditioned participation on measurable ROI and lead quality; they demanded clear ad labelling for paid slots.

  > "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya reacts to the announced merchant portal, including its verification, product listing, local-first matching, leads, dashboards, quotes and Partner slot."  

  > "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya said the Partner slot looks useful but it needs clear ROI metrics first, asking how to see when a link actually pays."  

  > "Kuching Home Appliance Centre says verified listings and local stores matched first sound good, but asks that before any small retailer commits to a paid Partner slot, cost per qualified lead be shown, the slot be labelled clearly as iklan front and centre, and the 'Best offer' badge be based on total cost (unit, delivery, installation, after-sales) and seller trust rather than on who paid."

- Stated intention: test the merchant portal, list verified items if CSV/upload and lead verification are manageable; wait for documented cost-per-qualified-lead and front‑labelled ads before buying Partner slots.

**Creators — will try and amplify only with consent, credit and transparent affiliate labelling**

- Creators reacted strongly to content-use and affiliate disclosure rules: many will test the app and use guest scans for content, but demand consent, creator credit and pre-click disclosure for affiliate links.

  > "Nadia Home Diary posted that the new app Casella just opened a public beta, takes a room photo or screenshot, tags furniture and electrical appliances with prices, and links to Shopee and Taobao."  

  > "Nadia Home Diary says 'best offer' must mean the total delivered home cost including item, shipping to Sabah and Sarawak, import tax and installation."  

  > "Dr. Salina Rahmat recounts that a small beauty creator wrote 'affiliate link — I earn a little if you buy, no pressure' before the link, which cost her a sale but led three followers to message that they trusted her more."  

  > "Vanessa Goh demands that platforms credit creators, get consent before use, and show the total landed cost (delivery plus installation plus import tax) rather than the sticker price."

- Stated intention: try and create (e.g., test 3 scans), but only endorse or upload images when credit/compensation and clear iklan/affiliate labelling are guaranteed.

**Professionals (small shops, installers, industry experts) — guarded endorsement tied to operational proof**

- Industry professionals pressed for measurable match accuracy, published benchmarks, and realistic delivery and installation coverage by postcode; they will not accept "92% match" badges as substitutes for SKU/model verification.

  > "Grace Chin agreed with the phrase 'No proof, no ringgit' and said one confident but wrong match is more expensive than no match, and that for large furniture 'Best offer' must mean total landed cost (unit + delivery by postcode + installation + after-sales), not the sticker price."  

  > "Halim Yaakob reported a Mount Austin customer bought a 1.5HP unit on a '92% match' that was a different outdoor unit series and excluded vacuum and breaker, and pressed for total installed price and clear affiliate labelling."

- Stated intention: test Casella’s merchant and benchmark features; recommend that merchants provide itemised quotes and that Casella publish match‑accuracy benchmarks and postcode-based delivery estimates before broad professional buy-in.

**Points of disagreement and friction that shaped intentions (and where tests are suggested)**

- Ad labelling on paid Partner slots: near‑universal merchant and community demand for front‑of‑click labels.

  > "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya demands that the Paid Partner slot be labelled IKLAN openly, before the click, in BM and English."  

  > "Muhammad Hazim agrees that the paid Partner slot must be labelled 'iklan' before the click."

  Suggestion (to test with real users): run a disclosure-timing A/B test (label-before-click vs label-after-click) to measure trust and click conversion (label as a suggestion, not a result).

- Privacy, retention and deletion: cautious users require a simple, demonstrable delete and explicit retention period before uploading real-home photos.

  > "Chua Li Ting asks whether she can try the app as a guest without signing in with her real name, and says she will not scan a single room if the retention period isn't clear."  

  > "Priya Nair advises testing the guest scan, sign-in, permissions, language, and privacy controls before deciding, and not giving the app more than it needs."

  Suggestion (to test): a short usability test showing the delete flow and retention policy to non-technical users and asking whether they feel comfortable uploading a real-home photo.

- Match accuracy vs sticker/tag reliability: appliance buyers and pros will abandon on a wrong first match.

  > "Ah Boon Fix It has beta-tested Casella and reviews gas and electrical appliances."  

  > "Ah Boon Fix It ... match accuracy is hit-or-miss, ... photos can be deleted but the option is buried 3 menus deep with no 'delete all'; the buy button opens Shopee/Taobao, making seller, courier and warranty holder three different parties."

  Suggestion (to test): publish per-class accuracy benchmarks and a top‑1 false‑match rate; run an independent labeled test set for appliances and bulky furniture and observe trust effects.

- Total landed cost definition and postcode variance: East Malaysian communities and buyers insist on postcode-based landed-costs.

  > "Sabah Sarawak Home Group tells East Malaysian homeowners to get local quotes, compare total landed cost, ask for realistic transit days to Sabah and Sarawak postcodes, and back contractor warnings with documentation."  

  > "Kuching Home Appliance Centre advises that for Sabah/Sarawak buyers always ask for the total landed cost by postcode, because import tax and delivery days are real and 'installation included conditions apply' often means not for East Malaysia."

  Suggestion (to test): simulate landed-cost calculations across representative postcodes (Peninsular vs Sabah vs Sarawak) and show users whether the app's landing-cost matches local quotes.

**Representative direct quotes used as behavioural evidence**

> "Guests get 3 free scans without an account, and saving items or a 4th scan asks them to sign in with Google, Apple, phone OTP or email."

> "Kevin Lim plans to measure first and then test Casella, and will delete Casella unless the first result is correct and has real reviews and delivery days."

> "Priya Nair reminds people to do a guest scan before signing in, reject unreasonable location permissions, check language settings and make sure data can be deleted."

> "Lau Kok Wai asks where room photos go, how long they are kept, whether deletion is actually permanent, and whether the guest scan works without an account or a phone number."

> "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya said the Partner slot looks useful but it needs clear ROI metrics first, asking how to see when a link actually pays."

> "Nadia Home Diary says 'best offer' must mean the total delivered home cost including item, shipping to Sabah and Sarawak, import tax and installation."

> "Ah Boon Fix It agrees 100% that any paid Partner slot must be clearly labeled as an advertisement and not hidden in the list."  

(Each quote above is taken verbatim from simulated agent posts in the simulation outputs.)

**Concluding predictive assessment (behaviours to expect in early rollout)**

- Expect many one‑off or exploratory tries driven by the 3 free guest scans (inspiration browsers, cautious guests and creators); retention beyond the guest scans depends heavily on proving match accuracy, showing itemised total landed cost by postcode, and providing a clear, demonstrable data‑deletion flow.

- Merchant uptake will be conditional: merchants will sign up and list if lead verification, CSV/listing ergonomics and clear cost‑per‑qualified‑lead metrics exist, and they will demand "iklan" labelling up front for any paid placement.

- Creators will test and amplify only under explicit credit/consent and pre‑click affiliate disclosure policies.

Where gaps remain in the simulation (insufficient evidence): direct platform-level split metrics for specific quotes (Twitter vs Reddit) were not consistently available for every quote in the retrieved results; any suggested tests above are proposals only, not measured outcomes.

## Points of contention and where groups disagree

**Overview of where groups disagree**

Posts and comments appeared across Twitter and Reddit (Twitter: 503 text items; Reddit: 335). The simulation produced repeated, concrete points of contention between homeowners, appliance buyers, cautious guests, creators, and local merchants. These disagreements cluster around (1) what "Best offer" should mean and whether it can be bought, (2) match accuracy vs. visual lookalikes, (3) guest-scan privacy, delete and retention, and (4) merchant monetisation (Partner slot, iklan labelling, and cost-per-lead). Below I synthesise those contested areas with direct citations from the simulated agents.

**What "Best offer" means — contested definition and non-purchasability**

Many voices insist the badge must reflect a verified, itemised total landed cost; others accept the badge only if the platform proves methodology. A persistent fault-line is between those who treat the badge as a helpful shortcut and those who treat it as a potential ad if not strictly governed.

> "Amirah Zulkifli says Casella is finally an app that shows total cost and not just the sticker price, and that the Best offer badge would be worth trying if it really includes delivery and installation."

> "Rumah Bajet MY says the 'Best offer' badge must not be purchasable and should be based on total landed cost and seller trust only."

> "Syafiq Hamdan says the 'Best offer' badge must not be purchasable and that only the total landed cost should count, with no proof meaning no ringgit."

> "Jason Reno Journal posted that the new Malaysian app Casella has opened a public beta, tags furniture and appliances with prices from a room photo or screenshot, links to Shopee and Taobao products, shows total price estimates including shipping, installation and import tax, and Taobao delivery is expected in 10 to 18 days."

Evidence shows consensus on the desired target (total landed cost), but disagreement over whether the badge might be influenced by paid placement or insufficient measurement. Multiple merchants and creators explicitly demand the badge be non-purchasable and tied to verifiable line items.

**Match accuracy vs. lookalike risk**

Content creators, industry professionals and technical-minded buyers disagree sharply on how Casella should present similarity/confidence and what disclosures are required.

> "Ah Boon Fix It says Casella's total cost estimate is a good idea but its match accuracy is hit-or-miss, showing in his video a kitchen photo suggesting a cabinet that does not fit and a sofa match that does not fit."

> "Farah Zainal requires that the Best offer badge never be buyable and always show total landed cost including unit, delivery to Sabah and Sarawak, installation, import tax and after-sales."

> "Jason Reno Journal asks the platform to publicly demand measured match accuracy, including top-1 versus retrieval precision and the false-match rate, instead of a '3 free scans' demo."

> "Grace Chin agreed with the phrase 'No proof, no ringgit' and said one confident but wrong match is more expensive than no match, and that for large furniture 'Best offer' must mean total landed cost (unit + delivery by postcode + installation + after-sales), not the sticker price."

Disagreement here is procedural: practitioners (e.g., Grace Chin, Jason Reno Journal) demand published benchmarks (per-class accuracy, false-match rates) before trusting the badge or confidence score; inspiration browsers and many homeowners treat visual matches as a starting point but not final. The conflict is not over the existence of a confidence score, but over the need for public, per-class methodology and the consequences of false positives for big-ticket items.

**Guest scans, privacy and deletion — who will use guest mode and under what guarantees**

Cautious users and privacy advocates demand strong, visible controls before uploading home photos; other users will trial guest scans but expect fast ways to delete data.

> "Priya Nair's routine is to guest scan first, check permissions, and reject location access without reason."

> "Chua Li Ting will not scan a single room unless retention terms are written clearly (hitam putih), and she wants to try as a guest without signing in with her real name."

> "Dr. Salina Rahmat requires a clear data-retention period, a permanent delete, and guest scan without handing over a phone number."

> "Budget Reno Bro advises screenshotting the total landed cost (unit, delivery by postcode, installation, tax), checking the full model code on the sticker instead of trusting a '92% match', and testing the delete button with a plant photo before uploading real home photos."

Tension: cautious guests insist on upfront, plain-language retention and deletion guarantees (and the ability to use guest scans without phone number). Many merchant and renovation communities treat guest scans as acceptable for discovery only — but they will not proceed to sign-ins or save photos until deletion and retention behaviours are proven. The disagreement is operational (what the app must display and how delete behaves) rather than ideological.

**Merchant portal, Partner slot and iklan labelling — paid placement vs. discovery**

Local merchants and marketplaces accept a paid Partner slot only under strict transparency and ROI accountability, while platform/business design assumes paid placement is a monetisation lever. This produces repeated friction.

> "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya said the Partner slot looks useful but it needs clear ROI metrics first, asking how to see when a link actually pays."

> "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya demands that the Paid Partner slot be labelled IKLAN openly, before the click, in BM and English."

> "Sinar Home Marketplace says a scan is a lead, not a sale, and Casella should publish top-1 match accuracy and false-match rate."

> "The Casella merchant phase includes one paid Partner slot per list that cannot receive the Best offer badge."

Merchants’ core friction points: (1) the Partner slot must be labelled IKLAN before the click; (2) small retailers require published cost-per-qualified-lead and lead verification; (3) the Best offer badge must remain unbuyable. The platform design that separates slot rules (e.g., partner slot cannot get the Best offer) reduces some conflict, but merchants still disagree on cost transparency and practical ROI.

**Platform-level fault lines and regional delivery/postcode disagreements**

East Malaysia (Sabah/Sarawak) and peninsula users disagree on how the app should treat cross‑sea logistics and whether a single landed-cost estimate is meaningful without postcode resolution.

> "Sabah Sarawak Home Group notes that one listing slot in the Casella app is a paid Partner slot that cannot get the 'Best offer' badge."

> "Sabah Sarawak Home Group advises East Malaysia members to verify the total landed cost themselves (unit price + shipping to their postcode + installation + local warranty coverage) and to check local KK and Kuching suppliers first, using Casella as a research tool, not a decision-maker."

> "Rosli Ahmad says total landed cost and the 'Best offer' badge must include real delivery days by postcode or state, not a 2-4 day promise for all of Malaysia."

Conflict: users in East Malaysia demand postcode-specific landed cost and transit times; platform-level claims of a total can mislead unless regional variance is explicit. This disagreement ties directly to the "Best offer" trust problem.

**Where groups explicitly disagree (thread-level examples)**

- On purchasability of the badge:
  > "Rumah Lengkap Marketing requires that the 'Best offer' badge not be purchasable and that it be based on total landed cost..."  
  vs. platform monetisation that includes a paid Partner slot (designed to be unbadged but still monetised).

- On the sufficiency of a confidence percentage:
  > "Budget Reno Bro found match accuracy hit-or-miss" and "Ah Boon Fix It says ... match accuracy is hit-or-miss"  
  vs. any casual user who may accept a "92% match" label without published benchmark.

- On disclosure timing:
  > "Nadia Home Diary says the paid Partner slot must be labelled 'iklan' before the click, not in the caption."  
  vs. any content model that only requires disclosure in captions or bios.

- On privacy controls:
  > "Chua Li Ting will not scan a single room unless retention terms are written clearly (hitam putih)..."  
  vs. users who will trial scans immediately (e.g., many inspiration browsers and guests using the 3 free scans).

**Unresolved questions and suggested tests (labelled as suggestions)**

The simulation exposes predictable disputes that need real-user experiments to resolve. The following are proposed tests (suggestions) — these are not results, only recommended validations:

1. Suggestion: A/B test "Best offer" presentation — one variant shows a single badge plus itemised landed-cost breakdown inline; the other shows only an itemised breakdown without a badge. Measure perceived trust and intent-to-contact (merchant lead) in controlled user panels.

2. Suggestion: Publish per-class accuracy benchmarks and run a user-facing transparency experiment: show top-1 category accuracy and false-match examples per category (furniture vs. small appliances vs. air-conditioners). Test whether published benchmarks change merchants’ willingness to accept the badge and buyers’ reliance on it.

3. Suggestion: Privacy-first flow test — implement guest-scan-only flow where no phone number is requested, a clear one-paragraph retention policy is shown, and a one-tap "permanent delete" works in under 10 seconds. Measure whether cautious users proceed beyond three scans and whether sign-ups increase after demonstrated deletions.

4. Suggestion: Paid Partner-slot disclosure and ROI pilot — run a merchant pilot where Partner slots are labelled IKLAN before the click (BM + English) and provide merchants with verified cost-per-qualified-lead and lead-to-sale conversion over 30 days. Collect qualitative feedback from small merchants on whether labelled slots harm, help or make no difference to lead quality.

5. Suggestion: Postcode-accurate landed-cost rollout test — for a subset of SKUs, calculate and display delivery and installation costs to five representative postcodes (Klang Valley, Penang, Kuching, Kota Kinabalu, rural Sarawak). Measure mismatch complaints and perceived accuracy among East Malaysia users.

**Short summary of the core contention**

- Universal agreement: total landed cost (unit + delivery by postcode + installation + import/tax + after-sales) matters and must be visible for purchase decisions.

- Core disputes: (1) How the "Best offer" badge is computed and whether it can be bought; (2) whether visual match scores without published benchmarks are trustworthy; (3) how and when merchants must label paid placements (IKLAN before click); and (4) whether privacy controls (guest use, retention, permanent delete) are sufficiently visible and trustworthy.

## Emergent trends, risks and suggested real‑world tests

**Emergent trends observed across the simulation**

- Broad, repeated conservatism: agents treat Casella primarily as a discovery/inspiration tool and reserve monetary commitment for when concrete line-item totals and verifiable match accuracy appear.

These disagreements determine which friction to prioritise for testing.

**Priority, actionable real‑world tests (each labelled 'Suggested test')**

Below are prioritized, small bounded experiments derived from agent concerns. Each test is described, the core success metric to observe, and which agents raised the need (quoted where available).

1) Suggested test — Guest privacy & delete-path usability (bounded prototype)
- What to test: Guest-mode flow from first scan through deletion for non‑signed users (no forced sign-up), including denial of location permission, visibility of retention policy, and an explicit, discoverable permanent-delete (and delete-all) action.
- Key metric(s): % of participants who (a) can find and execute permanent deletion as a guest within 3 minutes; (b) perception of whether deletion is permanent (qualitative).
- Who raised it: Priya Nair and Lau Kok Wai concerns.
- Evidence to cite:
  > "Priya Nair advises doing a guest scan before signing in, checking permissions, refusing location access without reason, checking language options, and ensuring data can be deleted."

  > "Lau Kok Wai says the deletion path must be testable by a guest, not only by account holders, because having to register just to have data removed is not privacy."

- Suggested protocol note: use a dummy photo (plant) first, observe behaviour, and follow up with a short survey asking whether users would upload a real home photo after the test.

2) Suggested test — Landed-cost clarity & Best offer trust A/B
- What to test: Show identical item matches with two treatments: A) Best offer badge that displays a fully itemised landed cost (unit + delivery to participant postcode + installation + warranty notes) and B) Best offer badge with sticker-only price plus a separate estimate. Randomise participants across household types (city vs East Malaysia postcode).
- Key metric(s): Relative change in willingness-to-request-quote or to click-through; incidence of follow-up questions about shipping/warranty; qualitative trust score.
- Who raised it: Amirah Zulkifli, Dr. Salina Rahmat, Budget Reno Bro.
- Evidence to cite:
  > "Amirah Zulkifli says Casella is finally an app that shows total cost and not just the sticker price..."

  > "Dr. Salina Rahmat recommends that Casella keep the 'Best offer' badge based on total landed cost and seller trust, never on who paid..."

- Suggested protocol note: include East Malaysia postcodes explicitly (Sabah/Sarawak) to capture logistic variance.

3) Suggested test — Disclosure timing for Partner slot and affiliate links (timing and format)
- What to test: Compare disclosure placements: (A) "IKLAN / ad" label shown before click and in BM+English; (B) disclosure shown only on landing page or in caption; (C) no disclosure. Use creators and ordinary shoppers as cohorts.
- Key metric(s): Creator willingness to share/endorse; end‑user trust rating and click-through change; complaints/negative feedback incidence.
- Who raised it: Nadia Home Diary, multiple merchant voices.
- Evidence to cite:
  > "Nadia Home Diary ... refuses to hide commissions: every link gets an 'iklan'/'Link affiliate' label before the click..."

  > "Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya demands that the Paid Partner slot be labelled IKLAN openly, before the click, in BM and English."

- Suggested protocol note: run with creators who record whether they will attach/endorse links under each disclosure condition.

4) Suggested test — Match‑accuracy tolerance & benchmark communication (bounded retrieval benchmark)
- What to test: Present users with matches at varied declared confidence levels (e.g., 60%, 80%, 92%), but accompany each with an explanation: (a) "category match" vs (b) "model-code match" and with a sample published false-match rate for that class. Measure how declared metrics and simple provenance statements (how test set built, per-class false-match rate) affect trust and action.
- Key metric(s): Change in willingness to accept the match for big-ticket items (sofa, aircond), % who request more verification, and qualitative reaction to each metric description.
- Who raised it: Jason Reno Journal, Grace Chin, Rumah Bajet MY.
- Evidence to cite:
  > "Jason Reno Journal asks the platform to publicly demand measured match accuracy, including top-1 versus retrieval precision and the false-match rate, instead of a '3 free scans' demo."

  > "Rumah Bajet MY said the benchmark must include precision@1 on model code, false-match rate and data provenance, and that '92% match' without a confidence score is decoration, not proof."

5) Suggested test — Merchant lead quality & cost‑per‑qualified‑lead pilot (30‑day bounded)
- What to test: Offer a small group of verified local merchants a 30-day Partner-slot trial with front-labelled IKLAN, tracking matched impressions → WhatsApp/quote leads → verified qualified leads (phone-confirmed). Share simple ROI dashboard for merchants.

**Operational notes and sequencing (what to test first and why)**

- Start with privacy & delete-path usability (Suggested test 1) and the disclosure-timing test (Suggested test 3). These are low-cost, high‑impact trust barriers that many agents said determine whether they would upload real photos or share links (and they reduce legal/PR risk quickly).
- Parallel small pilots for landed-cost clarity (Suggested test 2) and merchant cost-per-lead (Suggested test 5) — merchants will not buy into Partner slots without demonstrated cost-per-qualified-lead; buyers will not convert without clear landed totals.
- Run the match‑accuracy tolerance/benchmark communication test (Suggested test 4) with a cohort of technical reviewers and typical buyers for high-ticket categories; results determine whether to publish per-class benchmarks and how to surface confidence and provenance in the UI.
- Always include East Malaysia / postcode‑aware arms in price/lead tests (Suggested test 6) because multiple agents flagged logistic divergence as a conversion blocker.

**Minimum acceptance criteria (suggested, for each test)**
- Guest privacy & delete: 90% of test participants can find and execute permanent delete as guest within 3 minutes and understand the retention claim.
- Disclosure timing: creators will only attach/endorse links when pre-click iklan labels are present (measured as majority preference in creator cohort).
- Landed-cost clarity: itemised landed cost reduces “need to call shop” follow-ups by 40% in the test cohort and increases willingness-to-request-quote for considered items.
- Lead-quality pilot: merchants report a measurable, repeatable cost-per‑qualified‑lead and at least one merchant converts to a paid trial based on that metric.
- Benchmark communication: publishing per-class precision@1 and false-match rate increases trust enough that a targeted percentage of appliance buyers will proceed to verification steps rather than uninstalling after first mismatch.

**Evidence gaps and what the simulation cannot prove (and therefore must be tested with real people)**

- The simulation supplies agent intent and stated heuristics but not measured conversion, retention or actual lead-to-sale economics. Any acceptance thresholds above are suggestions to be validated.
- Per‑class, per‑region benchmark numbers for match accuracy are absent from the simulation and must be empirically measured in a controlled evaluation (Suggested test 4).
- Real merchant ROI on paid Partner slots requires live billing and verified lead tracking (Suggested test 5).
- Actual permanence of deletion (technical verification) and legal compliance must be tested in production rather than simulated flows (Suggested test 1).
